traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Portulacaceae with Hectorellaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves alternate or opposite; leaves simple; margins entire; veins pinnate or single; blades linear, lanceolate, oblanceolate, ovate or obovate; stipules usually present, rarely absent; plants usually hermaphrodite, sometimes polygamous; ovary usually superior, rarely half inferior; floral cup present or absent; stems woody or herbaceous; flowers solitary or in cymes; flowers actinomorphic or zygomorphic; perianth sepals and petals or tepals; fruit capsule; stamens 3 to 50; carpels (2-) 3 (-9). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.perianth.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Portulaca (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals 2, connate at the base; petals 4 or 5 (to 8 or more), free or shortly connate; FNA: petals 5-7, ephemeral.

traits.life_span.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Portulaca (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): herbs annual (perennial in P. suffrutescens); FOC vol. 5: annual or perennial. The family is Portulaca alone in the APG and WCVP sense.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Portulaca (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stems fleshy or suffrutescent; herbs.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Portulaca (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves alternate or opposite; FNA: alternate or subopposite; the genus file's NZ Flora reading agrees.

traits.leaf_division.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Portulacaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaf blade simple.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Portulacaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): margin entire.

traits.stipules.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Portulacaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): true stipules absent; nodes sometimes with axillary scales or hairs. FNA vol. 4: Portulaca's nodal hairs are regarded by some as stipular, a reading Geesink (1969) rejected.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Portulaca (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): a terminal head of sessile flowers, single or clustered, subtended by an involucre of leaves; FNA: terminal clusters or axillary on short branches.

traits.flowering_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Portulaca (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): inflorescences terminal in clusters, or axillary on short branches.

traits.bract_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Portulaca (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves congested and involucre-like just below the inflorescence.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Portulacaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers actinomorphic.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Portulaca (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals 4 or 5 (to 8 or more); FNA: 5-7.

traits.sexual_system.note: Flora of China vol. 5, Portulacaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers bisexual, very rarely unisexual.

traits.ovary_position.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Portulaca (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): ovary half inferior to inferior; FOC: half-inferior.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Portulaca (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens (4-)6-40(-100); FOC: 4-100.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Portulaca (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stigmas 3-8 (to 18), one per carpel; FOC family: 2-5-carpellate, stigma 2-9-lobed.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Portulaca (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): capsules membranaceous or chartaceous, circumscissile (a lid comes off).

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of North America vol. 4, Portulaca (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals fall from the top of the capsule (with the lid); FOC: persistent but inconspicuous.
